title: Continuous Two-Way Alignment
one_liner: Continuously reconcile system artifacts and their human-facing companion in both directions so neither machine progress nor human knowledge becomes an isolated, drifting truth.
problem: A useful companion starts drifting as soon as development continues. Code, configuration, tests and runtime state may move ahead while diagrams and explanations remain fixed. The reverse drift is just as damaging: people decide a target state, discover a constraint or learn from an incident in a meeting, chat or review, yet the executable system and its durable records never receive that knowledge. One-way generation solves only the first half and can overwrite interpretation; manual upkeep cannot match change volume; and declaring either side universally authoritative ignores that executable facts and human intent have different legitimate sources. Alignment therefore has competing forces: freshness versus review cost, automation versus semantic judgment, fast propagation versus stable shared views, and conflict visibility versus the temptation to choose a convenient winner silently.
solution: Define a versioned alignment contract between system artifacts and the Companion App. For every view or knowledge type, name its source, direction, trigger, owner, freshness objective and reconciliation rule. Artifact to companion: regenerate declared views from code, specifications, tests, runtime evidence and metadata; attach source versions or fingerprints; run change-triggered and scheduled checks; and expose drift sensors such as Wiki Pulse, age badges and commits-behind grades instead of a false binary current/stale label. Human to artifact: turn decisions, corrected explanations, target-state changes and learning opportunities into durable ADRs, Decision History entries, specifications, tests, tasks, code or metadata through a reviewable write-back queue. Never silently overwrite either side when claims conflict. Present the conflict with evidence, assign an owner and record the resolution so the alignment process itself leaves history. Run the loop continuously through agent-pipelines and scheduled-quality-sweeps, with Quality Review checking semantic coherence beyond hashes. Agent Studio provides operating evidence: Wiki Pulse and drift grading expose artifact-to-companion lag, Quality Review challenges meaning, and the 24 July target-state consolidation demonstrates human knowledge being carried back into the durable system. The consequence is not permanent agreement but observable, bounded divergence and a practiced route back to alignment; teams gain trustworthy freshness signals and durable learning in exchange for review queues, ownership and reconciliation work. This is the operating counterpart of companion-app; it extends the existing spec-drift meta-loop, uses sidecar-metadata for fingerprints and review state, and writes rationale through decision-memory rather than creating a second decision store.
